description: This figure is a single rendered table (Table 1) — no plot, micrograph, spectrum or schematic — listing three vacuum-cast austenitic Fe–Ni–Cr steels. The rows are labelled Base, 2.5 Si and 2.5 Al; the columns are Alloy, C, N, Ni, Cr, Mn, Si, Al and "Annealing Temp. (°C)", with the composition values given in wt.%. The Base alloy reads C 0.028, N 0.0034, Ni 15.05, Cr 11.06, Mn 1.09, Si 0.002, Al 0.05, annealed at 1040 °C. The 2.5 Si alloy reads C 0.028, N 0.0036, Ni 14.99, Cr 10.98, Mn 1.10, Si 2.50, Al 0.06, annealed at 1075 °C. The 2.5 Al alloy reads C 0.030, N 0.0034, Ni 15.04, Cr 11.02, Mn 1.08, Si 0.034, Al 2.47, annealed at 1060 °C. The table therefore shows that the three steels are compositionally nearly identical except for a deliberate ~2.5 wt.% addition of either Si or Al, and that each was solution annealed at a slightly different temperature. It is the compositional basis for the later lattice-parameter and stacking-fault-energy comparisons.

subfigures.description: Single rendered data table (Table 1) with a header row (Alloy, C, N, Ni, Cr, Mn, Si, Al, Annealing Temp. (°C)) and three data rows: Base, 2.5 Si and 2.5 Al. All composition entries are wt.%; annealing temperature is given in °C.

observations.observation: The image is a single rendered table with column headers Alloy, C, N, Ni, Cr, Mn, Si, Al and 'Annealing Temp. (°C)'; compositions are in wt.%.
The Base alloy row lists Si = 0.002 and Al = 0.05 wt.%.
The 2.5 Si alloy row lists Si = 2.50 and Al = 0.06 wt.%.
The 2.5 Al alloy row lists Si = 0.034 and Al = 2.47 wt.%.
The three annealing temperatures printed in the table differ: Base 1040 °C, 2.5 Si 1075 °C, 2.5 Al 1060 °C.
Ni is 15.05, 14.99 and 15.04 wt.% and Cr is 11.06, 10.98 and 11.02 wt.% for Base, 2.5 Si and 2.5 Al respectively.
Mn is ~1.08-1.10 wt.%, C is 0.028-0.030 wt.% and N is 0.0034-0.0036 wt.% in all three alloys.
The caption states that this is Table 1, 'Experimental steel compositions (wt.%) and solution annealing temperatures'.
The citing text states the three austenitic steel compositions are all approximately the same except for variations in Al and Si alloying.

The citing text states the steels were vacuum cast, homogenized for 20 h at 1200 °C, hot rolled and then annealed for 1 h at the temperatures indicated in Table 1 to achieve coarse grain sizes of approximately 140 µm.
The citing text states the compositions were derived from a microstructure survey of the Fe–Ni–Cr–Al–Si system [30].
The citing text states '2.5 Si' and 'base' differ in Si content and the two Al-containing alloys differ in Al content, so relative alloying is defined by these differences.
